title: Second-order gap for online selection of a monotone subsequence
short_statement: For online selection of an increasing subsequence from $n$ i.i.d. continuous observations, the optimal expected length is $\sqrt{2n}-O(\log n)$. Does the second-order gap $g(n)=\sqrt{2n}-\mathbb{E}L_n^*$ diverge, or is it bounded?
open_problem: Determine the asymptotic behavior of $g(n)=\sqrt{2n}-\mathbb{E}L_n^*$ for the optimal online increasing-subsequence policy; in particular, decide whether $g(n)\to\infty$ or $g(n)=O(1)$.
full_statement: Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be independent observations from a common continuous distribution, revealed one at a time. An online policy must irrevocably accept or reject each $X_t$, and the accepted values must form an increasing subsequence. Let $L_n^*$ be the length selected by an optimal online policy. Distribution-freeness reduces the model to $X_t\sim\mathrm{Unif}[0,1]$. The classical first-order asymptotic is $\mathbb{E}L_n^*\sim \sqrt{2n}$, and the best general bounds give $\sqrt{2n}-O(\log n)\le \mathbb{E}L_n^*\le \sqrt{2n}$. Arlotto, Wei, and Xie give a simple adaptive policy within $2(\log n+1)$ of optimal and ask for a sharper understanding of the second-order correction. The core open problem is whether the deficit $g(n)=\sqrt{2n}-\mathbb{E}L_n^*$ diverges with $n$, as the logarithmic upper bound allows, or remains bounded.
known_results: Samuels and Steele established the $\sqrt{2n}$ first-order law. Bruss and Robertson gave the upper bound $\mathbb{E}L_n^*\le \sqrt{2n}$, and Bruss-Delbaen/Arlotto-Nguyen-Steele developed the matching lower bound up to $O(\log n)$ and central-limit behavior in related Poissonized/discrete settings. Arlotto, Wei, and Xie construct an explicit adaptive policy with expected length at least $\sqrt{2n}-2(\log n+1)$. They also report numerical evidence suggesting that their policy may be within a constant of optimal, but the simplest stated open question remains whether $g(n)$ diverges.

where_posed.text: Concluding remarks of Arlotto, Wei, and Xie, 'An adaptive O(log n)-optimal policy for the online selection of a monotone subsequence from a random sample'.
